[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Technical Tutorial: Diffusion Models (DDPM, Score-based models, Classifier-free guidance)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Diffusion probabilistic models have emerged as the state-of-the-art framework for generative modeling in deep learning, outperforming traditional GANs in sample quality and training stability. This tutorial covers the mathematical foundations and implementation mechanics of Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM), Score-based generative models, and Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG)."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"1. Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"DDPMs are parameterized Markov chains trained to produce data by reversing a forward diffusion process. The forward process gradually adds Gaussian noise to the data x_0 according to a predefined variance schedule beta_1, ..., beta_T."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Forward Process: q(x_t | x_{t-1}) = N(x_t; sqrt(1 - beta_t) * x_{t-1}, beta_t * I)"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Closed-form sampling at arbitrary timestep t: q(x_t | x_0) = N(x_t; sqrt(alpha_bar_t) * x_0, (1 - alpha_bar_t) * I), where alpha_t = 1 - beta_t and alpha_bar_t = product from s=1 to t of alpha_s."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

def q_sample(x_0, t, sqrt_alphas_cumprod, sqrt_one_minus_alphas_cumprod, noise=None):
    if noise is None:
        noise = torch.randn_like(x_0)
    sqrt_alpha_bar = sqrt_alphas_cumprod[t].view(-1, 1, 1, 1)
    sqrt_one_minus_alpha_bar = sqrt_one_minus_alphas_cumprod[t].view(-1, 1, 1, 1)
    return sqrt_alpha_bar * x_0 + sqrt_one_minus_alpha_bar * noise"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Reverse Process and Loss Function"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"The reverse process is parameterized by a neural network p_theta(x_{t-1} | x_t). Rather than predicting the mean directly, Ho et al. showed that training the network to predict the added noise epsilon at step t yields superior results. The simplified training objective is expressed as an expectation over timesteps and noise."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"def p_losses(model, x_0, t, sqrt_alphas_cumprod, sqrt_one_minus_alphas_cumprod, noise=None):
    if noise is None:
        noise = torch.randn_like(x_0)
    x_noisy = q_sample(x_0, t, sqrt_alphas_cumprod, sqrt_one_minus_alphas_cumprod, noise)
    predicted_noise = model(x_noisy, t)
    loss = F.mse_loss(predicted_noise, noise)
    return loss"},{"order":11,"type":"heading","text":"2. Score-Based Generative Models"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Score-based models view generative learning through the lens of estimating the score function of the data distribution, defined as the gradient of the log probability density with respect to the data: s_theta(x) = gradient_x * log p(x). This avoids the need to compute normalizing constants."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Denoising Score Matching: Trains a neural network to predict the score of noise-perturbed data distributions across multiple noise scales."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs): Song et al. generalized both DDPM and score-based models using continuous-time SDEs, where the forward process is a diffusion SDE and generation is handled via the corresponding reverse-time SDE."},{"order":15,"type":"heading","text":"3. Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG)"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Conditional generation allows guiding diffusion models using text prompts or class labels. Classifier-Free Guidance eliminates the need for a separate auxiliary classifier by jointly training a conditional and unconditional diffusion model within a single neural network (often by randomly dropping the conditioning context with a probability like p = 0.1)."},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"During sampling, the final noise prediction is extrapolated away from the unconditional prediction toward the conditional prediction using a guidance scale w."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"def compute_cfg_noise(model, x_t, t, context, null_context, guidance_scale):
    # Concatenate conditional and unconditional inputs for parallel batch processing
    x_in = torch.cat([x_t, x_t], dim=0)
    t_in = torch.cat([t, t], dim=0)
    context_in = torch.cat([context, null_context], dim=0)
    
    # Model outputs predicted noise
    noise_pred = model(x_in, t_in, context_in)
    noise_cond, noise_uncond = noise_pred.chunk(2, dim=0)
    
    # Apply Classifier-Free Guidance formula
    guided_noise = noise_uncond + guidance_scale * (noise_cond - noise_uncond)
    return guided_noise"},{"order":19,"type":"heading","text":"Summary"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"DDPMs provide a discrete Markov chain foundation using reparameterized noise targets. Score-based models generalize this concept to continuous-time SDEs and score matching. Finally, Classifier-Free Guidance acts as a crucial inference-time mechanism to boost prompt adherence and semantic alignment in modern text-to-image architectures like Stable Diffusion."}]
